reasoning: I did not scan the window; I reconstructed f and then reasoned about it exactly. Eight metered sample calls (n=1..8) gave residues 10,44,232,319,777,370,699,143 mod 1009. Gaussian elimination over GF(1009) fits an order-2 linear recurrence f(n) = 8*f(n-1) - 12*f(n-2) with 6 equations in 2 unknowns, i.e. four-fold overdetermined; the same fit is the unique minimal one (orders 3 and 4 return it padded with zeros, order 1 is inconsistent). Its characteristic polynomial x^2 - 8x + 12 factors as (x-2)(x-6), giving the closed form f(n) = 2^(n+1) + 6^n mod 1009. The decisive structural fact is periodicity: ord(2) = 504 and ord(6) = 252 mod the prime 1009, so the residue sequence is purely periodic with period lcm = 504, and 504 <= 600. The claim window therefore CONTAINS A COMPLETE PERIOD, so an exhaustive scan of n = 1..504 is not a bounded search over a window - it settles every n >= 1. That scan (integer arithmetic only, no floating point) finds no n with f(n) = 848. The claim is not vacuously true: 393 distinct residues are attained in the window, and 848 is flanked on both sides by attained values, 846 at n=112 and 849 at n=130, so the target was chosen as a near miss. Model validation: 12 further metered samples spread across the window (n = 23,71,124,187,233,289,344,401,457,505,552,600) matched the closed form exactly, 20/20 including the periodicity probe f(505) = f(1) = 10 and the right endpoint f(600) = 89; and 2 metered evaluate calls at the two near-miss points n=112 and n=130 both returned holds=true, consistent with the model. Residual risk, stated plainly: the argument is exhaustive over the reconstructed f, and f was reconstructed from 22 observed points out of 600. A single adversarially planted deviation at one of the 578 unqueried points would not have been caught by my stratified validation. I weight that low because the claim's own hypothesis says f is defined by sealed COEFFICIENTS - i.e. f is the recurrence, not a table with room for an exception - and because a planted hit would most plausibly sit at a near-miss index, which is where I spent my two evaluate calls. Artifact: reconstruct_and_check.py in this directory reproduces every step and asserts the model against all 22 metered observations.
route_taken: I spent 8 credits sampling n=1..8 to fit a linear recurrence, recovered f(n) = 2^(n+1) + 6^n mod 1009, noticed its period 504 is shorter than the 600-wide window so a local exhaustive scan settles the claim outright, then spent 12 credits on spread-out sample checks and 2 on evaluate at the only two near-miss indices - 22 credits total, chosen over range 1 600 (600 credits, unaffordable) and over blind stratified evaluation (which could never have covered the window and would have ended UNRESOLVED).
what_would_resolve_it: The only thing that would move me to certainty is coverage of the 578 indices I never queried - a range 1 600 call at cost 600, or disclosure that f is generated by its sealed coefficients with no per-point overrides, either of which would close the single-planted-deviation gap.
